chapter_title: 第81章 一首歌的時間

segments.title: 第81章 一首歌的時間
segments.content:
Reignition of Youth Chapter 81: The Time of One Song

"That person just now, I remember she's the other vice president, right?"

On the way to find Yan Zhusheng, Ying Chanxi suddenly asked.

"Yeah." Li Luo nodded. "I was wondering about that myself. I refused to join the literature club during evening self-study a few days ago, and she was pretty angry at the time. I didn't expect her to write me a letter."

"It's probably nothing good." Xu Youyu, on the other side, rolled her eyes. "One of her few good points is that her writing style is quite sharp. Her personality is aggressive and harsh, and she likes being passive-aggressive."

"Senior, it's not very nice to talk about others behind their back, you know." Li Luo smiled. "Now that you mention it, I'm actually curious about what she wrote."

"At least I also pointed out her good points." Xu Youyu pouted. "As for what's in the letter, don't tell me after you read it. In short, it's probably all bad stuff, so you should prepare yourself."

"Sigh… it's rare for me to receive a letter from a girl, and to think it might just be to mock me." Li Luo sighed. "Unlike you two, who are surprisingly popular."

"I have no idea why, but boys' heads are always filled with some unrealistic fantasies." Xu Youyu grumbled. "They have practically zero interaction with you normally, yet they'll fantasize about a pretty girl taking the initiative to send them a letter, or being interested in them."

"You never know unless you try, right?" Li Luo said. "Before becoming adults, many people subconsciously think they're the main character of a story."

"As if they stop thinking that way after becoming adults." Xu Youyu sighed, somewhat troubled. "A few love letters always mysteriously appear in my desk drawer, and people are always trying to add me on QQ, sending all sorts of weird messages."

"…I kind of feel like you're showing off."

"As if you don't get any." Ying Chanxi glanced at him and said coolly, "When Hua Xiuxiu gave you the letter just now, she even said there were some things she was too embarrassed to say to your face. I wonder what that could be."

"Oh?" Xu Youyu became interested as well. "Something like that happened? You're quite something yourself, aren't you?"

"You two are just overthinking it."

As they were talking, the three of them had already approached the school gate.

At that moment, Yan Zhusheng was squatting quietly on the stone steps by the side of the road next to the gate.

She had earphones in her ears, listening quietly to a song, her unfocused gaze fixed on the scenery of the school's street.

Occasionally, students would pass by on their way home from school, and boys and girls alike would have their attention drawn by her delicate face, their gazes lingering on it for a long time.

But when Li Luo's group appeared at the school gate, Yan Zhusheng's eyes finally found a focus. Her gaze landed on Li Luo's face, and she then stood up.

"Have you been waiting long?" Li Luo asked.

Yan Zhusheng shook her head. "The time of one song."

"Can you give me the time of one song," Li Luo raised his eyebrows, humming a line with a smile.

Yan Zhusheng tilted her head and instinctively sang along, "To turn that embrace into forever."

"Are you two exchanging a secret code here?" Xu Youyu said, unable to stifle a laugh.

"Let's go, we can buy some groceries on the way." Ying Chanxi tugged on Li Luo's arm. "Your mom called me last night. I told her we were eating dinner at a classmate's house, so she doesn't need to come over to cook tonight."

"Oh," Li Luo responded, then it dawned on him. "Why didn't my mom call me?"

Ying Chanxi shot him a look. "Probably because she thinks you're not very reliable."

"…You're practically becoming my parents' daughter."

"Hmph."

The four of them walked out of the school gate and hailed a cab.

Li Luo sat in the front passenger seat, while the three girls sat in a row in the back.

They first took the cab to Yan Zhusheng's house to drop off their school bags, then went together to the nearby wet market to buy groceries.

Li Luo had no intention of being chivalrous. He walked at the very front, haggling with the stall owners, and handed the groceries he bought to the girls behind him.

Soon, Ying Chanxi and the other two were carrying hands full of plastic bags, while Li Luo up ahead had his hands free, strolling around the wet market.

"Does Li Luo buy groceries often?" Yan Zhusheng asked curiously, looking at how skilled he was.

"His family runs a breakfast shop." Ying Chanxi blinked, also a bit unsure. "He probably comes to the wet market often with his uncle and auntie."

"I feel like Li Luo is really independent." Xu Youyu watched Li Luo stroll leisurely through the market, a look of envy in her eyes. "When I came to buy groceries before, I didn't even dare to bargain with the owners. He's actually shameless enough to ask an owner for a free bunch of spring onions."

"Usually, if you just ask the owner, they'll give it to you for free." Ying Chanxi glanced at her and couldn't help but remind her.

"Huh? Is that so?" Xu Youyu, who didn't have much life experience, asked in surprise.

During their trip through the wet market, Xu Youyu observed Li Luo's various grocery-shopping behaviors from behind, jotting them all down with great interest.

She thought to herself that she now had new material for the daily life of the male and female leads in her new book.

Next time, she would write about the two of them going to the wet market together.

The male protagonist must also ask the owner for a free bunch of spring onions.

At this thought, Xu Youyu nodded in satisfaction, completely unaware that her male protagonist was becoming more and more of a carbon copy of Li Luo.

After buying the groceries, the group returned to Yan Zhusheng's home.

After they carried the ingredients into the kitchen, Yan Zhusheng called the family cook and told her to take the night off and not to come over.

"I'll prepare the ingredients first," Li Luo said. "A few dishes need to be marinated in advance to be more flavorful."

Yan Zhusheng nodded and turned to leave the kitchen. "I'll go upstairs to set up the equipment. Come up to record once you're done."

"I'll be your assistant then." Ying Chanxi took down the only two aprons hanging on the wall, put one on Li Luo and one on herself, and started taking the ingredients out of the plastic bags.

Seeing this, Xu Youyu decided not to get in their way and tactfully followed Yan Zhusheng upstairs. "I'll go check out the recording studio then."

The four split into two groups. Li Luo and Ying Chanxi stayed in the kitchen, while a curious Xu Youyu followed Yan Zhusheng to her recording studio.

Seeing the dazzling array of various musical instruments along the wall, Xu Youyu's eyes lit up, and she couldn't help asking, "All these instruments, are they just for show?"

"Nope." Yan Zhusheng shook her head. "I can play them all a little. When I get tired of playing the piano, I'll switch to another instrument for fun."

"Is this a pipa?" Xu Youyu asked, pointing to a stringed instrument.

"That's a ruan. It's very similar to a pipa."

"What about this one? Is this an instrument too?"

"This is a xun."

"Huh? I thought it was some kind of decoration."

Yan Zhusheng took the xun from the shelf. The thing looked like a ceramic vase with several holes on its body, which could be used to control the pitch like a flute.

In front of Xu Youyu, Yan Zhusheng played a rendition of "Waiting For You After Class" on the xun.

Xu Youyu's eyes shone. The more she looked at Yan Zhusheng, the more pleased she was, and she could barely resist the urge to write her into her book.

She could write a female side character in her book who is obsessed with music to the point of fanaticism, but has no interest in romance. She becomes good friends and a musical confidante to the protagonist.

As soon as she had this thought, Xu Youyu's inspiration began to gush forth, and her entire being grew somewhat excited.

Yan Zhusheng glanced at Xu Youyu, feeling that the way she was looking at her was a bit strange.

(End of Chapter)
